markdown_report:
The best first experiment is a **prefix-aligned BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter**. At 0% research progress, establishing trustworthy measurements should precede architectural changes. No measured results were supplied.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Current margins measure training reconstruction. They cannot establish appended-mask next-item performance. (2) Broad relevance dominates the qualitative feedback. This motivates testing recent-history dependence, but does not establish users’ ownership or current needs. (3) Missing samples currently produce healthy-looking zeros. Counts and unavailable results are necessary for reliable interpretation.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) motivates masked supervision and appended-mask inference. Its training/deployment distinction makes prefix-aligned probes essential. (2) [Robust Training](https://iris.uniroma1.it/bitstream/11573/1740238/1/Siciliano_Robust-Training_2024.pdf) motivates history-removal interventions. Transfer from its studied architectures to BERT4Rec remains untested here. (3) [Interpreting User Inaction](https://will-qianzhao.github.io/pubs/zhao2018recsys-a.pdf) distinguishes reasons for nonselection. Unidentified or deferred items therefore should not become rejection labels.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Evidence | Gap addressed |
|---|---|---|
| Contract integrity | Mask provenance, readout and reload checks | Invalid diagnostic scores |
| Behavioral sensitivity | Paired recent/older-history removal | Unclear history dependence |
| Feedback interpretation | Explicit statements and available text | Rejection versus uncertainty |

**Candidate algorithms.** Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment by dimension |
|---|---|---|
| Prefix-aligned contract adapter [BERT4Rec] | 4/8/4 | Originality: integrates useful checks; components are established. Potential: enables reliable evolution; alone cannot improve ranking. Difficulty: reuses ModelView; provenance needs sampler support. |
| Paired recency sensitivity probe [Robust Training] | 5/7/5 | Originality: controlled BERT4Rec adaptation; removal tests already exist. Potential: guides masking choices; sensitivity need not imply preference quality. Difficulty: shares inference; repeated scoring adds cost. |
| Evidence-coded feedback audit [User Inaction] | 4/6/3 | Originality: connects uncertainty to diagnosis; taxonomy is established. Potential: prevents false rejection labels; feedback is sparse. Difficulty: simple schema; evidence adjudication remains manual. |

**Selected algorithm.** Preserve the corrected BERT4Rec and add an integrity gate followed by training-only prefix diagnostics. Withhold an observed training interaction, retain only its preceding history, reserve one position for the mask, left-pad, and score the mask representation. Compare live and checkpoint-reloaded predictor logits on identical inputs. Test short, full-length and empty histories; use deliberately corrupted masking/readout as structural positive controls.

Then compare original prefixes with equal-sized recent and older removals using identical candidates. Report target-rank changes, margin changes, sample counts and user-bootstrap intervals; these diagnose model sensitivity, not causal user preferences. Preserve both adapter entry points and ModelView compatibility. Report unavailable quantities explicitly, leave category-metadata breakdowns empty, and keep selection exclusively on unchanged macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Implement a prefix-aligned diagnostic adapter that verifies BERT4Rec training/inference integrity before measuring history sensitivity. Retain exactly one independently trained BERT4Rec model per category.
idea.motivation: Current training-position margins can obscure deployment mismatch, and empty samples can appear healthy. Qualitative feedback motivates investigating recent-history dependence, but supplies no numerical evidence that recency interventions will improve HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces. Inspect masking provenance through optional sampler instrumentation without changing the loader's four-element tuple; report provenance checks unavailable when instrumentation is absent. Do not infer leakage merely from repeated item IDs. Construct diagnostic prefixes exclusively from training histories. Match the deployed predictor's truncation, positions and appended-mask convention, and use the greatest nonpadding index, never count minus one. Compare reloaded and live logits with dropout disabled and documented numerical tolerances. Exclude padding and mask embeddings from collapse checks. Use null with a reason and sample count for unavailable measurements. Keep unavailable metadata breakdowns empty. Preserve four-category routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Any future architecture change must also change the embedded predictor writer. This proposal introduces diagnostics, not an unverified replacement for the unavailable baseline source.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
  def run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save model mode; set evaluation mode
    initialize metrics, definitions, counts, unavailable_reasons
    check reserved tokens, padding exclusion and bidirectional attention
    check supervised-position masking using provenance if available
    run structural positive controls for exposed shifted targets,
      omitted appended masks and incorrect count-minus-one readout
    for eligible training user and withheld training position:
      target = history[position]
      prefix = history[:position]
      inputs = left_pad(truncate(prefix, L-1) + [MASK], L)
      readout = greatest index where inputs != PAD
      candidates = fixed seeded diagnostic candidates including target
      compare live scores with checkpoint-reloaded predictor scores
      record target rank and positive-negative margins
      k = feasible fixed removal size
      if recent and older removals are both eligible:
        score both edited prefixes on the same candidates
        record paired changes and eligibility counts
    aggregate by dataset, history length and training popularity
    bootstrap users with all their prefixes grouped together
    restore model mode
    return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
  embed measured metrics, definitions, counts and unavailable reasons
  request evidence-linked findings, explicitly separating structural
  failures, training-only sensitivity and unchanged host validation

originality.positive: Combines BERT4Rec-specific integrity checks and paired behavioral probes within the existing diagnostic interface.
originality.negative: Masking checks, prediction parity and history interventions are established techniques rather than new learning principles.

future_potential.positive: Provides reliable evidence for subsequent single-model masking and architecture experiments.
future_potential.negative: Better diagnostics alone do not establish an improvement in validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Most scoring and aggregation can reuse ModelView and the existing probe.
code_difficulty.negative: Mask provenance, checkpoint parity and edge-case controls require careful integration with the supplied baseline.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Provides the masked-item bidirectional recommendation backbone and appended-mask prediction approach underlying the proposal.
limitations: Does not establish the correctness of this host's sampler, padding, checkpoint writer or diagnostic implementation.

related_work.title: Robust Training (2024; supplied search result)
contributions: Motivates measuring ranking sensitivity to removal of recent interactions.
limitations: The supplied summary concerns GRU/SASRec variants; applicability to BERT4Rec requires measurement.
Ranking sensitivity does not establish causal changes in user preference.

related_work.title: Interpreting User Inaction
contributions: Motivates distinguishing deferred interest and other reasons for nonselection from explicit rejection.
limitations: Does not provide preference labels for the four Amazon datasets or justify inferring unobserved ownership, mood or intent.
